subtopics.title: Three Highs by Name, Place and Character

questions.question: The three subtropical high-pressure cells affecting South Africa are the:
options: South Atlantic High, South Indian High and Kalahari High
Benguela High, Agulhas High and Karoo High
Cape High, Natal High and Highveld High
Azores High, Siberian High and Kalahari High

questions.question: In the Southern Hemisphere, air circulates around a high-pressure cell:
options: Anticlockwise in summer, clockwise in winter

questions.question: Anticyclones produce clear, dry weather because:
options: They contain no water vapour at all
Their air subsides, warming adiabatically and dissolving cloud

questions.question: Which high is seasonal in strength and height, dominating at the surface in winter?

subtopics.title: How the Highs Run South Africa's Seasons

questions.question: In winter, the interior plateau stays dry because the inversion layer:
options: Sits below the level of the escarpment, blocking moist ocean air from the plateau

questions.question: Summer thunderstorms occur over the interior because:
options: The inversion drops to ground level
Cold fronts cross the plateau daily
The Kalahari High weakens and lifts, letting moist South Indian High air flood in below a raised inversion

questions.question: The Western Cape receives winter rainfall because the pressure belt:
options: Strengthens over the Cape in winter
Shifts north with the sun, letting mid-latitude cold fronts swing under the continent

questions.question: When the South Atlantic High ridges around the southern tip of the country, the south coast experiences:
options: Cool, moist onshore flow bringing cloud, drizzle and rain

subtopics.title: The Travelling Disturbances — Moisture Front, Coastal Low, Berg Wind

questions.question: The moisture front over the summer interior is the boundary between:
options: Moist tropical air from the north and east and dry hot air over the west

questions.question: Ahead of a coastal low, the coast typically experiences:
options: Hot, dry, offshore airflow drawn down from the plateau

questions.question: A berg wind is hot and dry because the air:
options: Descends more than a kilometre off the plateau, warming adiabatically at about one degree per hundred metres
Passes over the warm Agulhas current

questions.question: Berg-wind days are the country's peak fire-danger days because they combine:
options: Dry fuel, very low humidity and strong gusty wind

subtopics.title: Reading It All on the Synoptic Chart

questions.question: A synoptic chart showing a strong high over the interior with fronts brushing the far south is most likely a:
The ridging signature on a chart is:
options: The South Atlantic High's isobars bulging eastward around the south coast after a front clears
A closed low over the Kalahari
Isobars packed tightly around the escarpment
A trough line over the Highveld

questions.question: On a summer satellite image, the moisture front appears as:
options: A circular cloud mass with an eye
A comma-shaped band over the Cape
A diagonal north-west to south-east line of thunderstorm cloud across the interior
A fog bank along the west coast

questions.question: Coastal station reports showing hot, dry, offshore winds indicate:
options: The passage of a warm front
Berg-wind conditions, with an abrupt cool change likely as the coastal low or front passes

questions.question: In the three-guards picture, the guards stand for:
options: The South Atlantic High, the South Indian High and the Kalahari High

questions.question: Sinking air destroys weather because as it sinks it:
options: Gets squashed, warms up and eats clouds like morning sun eats mist

questions.question: The west-coast guard explains why:
options: The sea at Blouberg is freezing, the west coast gets fog, and the Namib is a desert

questions.question: In the pot-lid picture, the lid stands for:
options: The inversion layer of warm air that stops rising air from climbing through

questions.question: In winter the plateau stays dry because the lid:
options: Sits below the escarpment, so moist sea air cannot climb the step onto the plateau

questions.question: The brown winter haze over the townships in July is:
options: Dust and smoke trapped under the low winter inversion lid

questions.question: The four-o'clock Highveld summer storm happens because:
options: The berg wind blows every afternoon
Moist air over baking ground rises freely once the lid has lifted above the escarpment

subtopics.title: The Hairdryer Wind and the Cool Change

questions.question: The berg wind is called the hairdryer because plateau air:
options: Falls over a kilometre toward the sea, warming about one degree per hundred metres, and arrives hot, dry and gusty
Is heated by the warm ocean
Blows in circles like a fan

questions.question: The east coast records its strangest heat — thirty-plus degrees in July — during:
Behind the coastal low — the sliding bead — the coast experiences:
options: Cool damp sea air sweeping in, with cloud, drizzle and a sharp temperature drop

questions.question: The full chain that ties the topic together is:
options: Equator, poles, jet stream, trade winds
Guards build the setup, the lid stores hot dry air, and the travelling systems — hairdryer and bead — release it
